newsitem.title: USA: Uncle B's says well-positioned to expand products.
newsitem.headline: Uncle B's says well-positioned to expand products.

text.p: Uncle B's Bakery Inc said on Friday it is "well-positioned" to expand its product and customer base.

"As we near the completion of our plant expansion, I am confident we have made a series of excellent strategic decisions that will enable Uncle B's to build upon its success in this quarter, and that the company is well-positioned to expand its product and customer base," said William Rose, chairman/chief executive officer, in an earnings statement.
It reported Friday first-quarter 1996 net earnings of $0.08 per share versus $0.04 pre-charge net a year earlier.

The year-ago charge reflected a change in accounting for new account allowances from the capitalization method to expensing costs as incurred. Including that charge, 1995 first-quarter per-share net income showed a $0.35 loss.
First-quarter 1996 net sales rose to a record $6.4 million versus $4.0 million in the year-ago period, the company said.

Rose tied first-quarter 1996 gains to reduced "inefficiencies" related to plant expansion and new product manufacturing. He also said the company had lowered its general and administrative costs, while overall plant efficiencies continued to improve.
Uncle B's Bakery makes and markets never-frozen bagels.
